Lookup of HTML named character references and numeric references.

entityToRune converts an entity body ("amp", "Uuml", "#65", "#x41") to a Rune, or Rune(0) when it is unknown. entityToUtf8 returns the UTF-8 text, or "" when it is unknown. Names are case-sensitive and do not include the leading & or the trailing ;.

Both procs accept a string and an openArray[char] view. View overload avoids copying when the caller already has a slice.

The checked-in table reproduces the values shipped before the generated lookup. See tools/gen_entitydata.nims for the data source and for the differences from the current spec.

Data and lookup

buildEntityTables turns the checked-in table into immutable tables at compile time: a 4,096-slot open-addressed table, a concatenated name pool, the distinct code-point values, and a 256-entry associated-values table. The lookup uses a gperf-style hash over the length and the first, second and last byte, with linear probing and a full name comparison.

Numeric forms

Decimal and hexadecimal forms are parsed directly from the input view on Nim 2.x. The Nim 1.6 fallback copies the short numeric slice. The grammar matches the previous implementation: underscores are allowed, hex accepts optional 0x and # prefixes, signs are not accepted where the old code rejected them, and the full input must be consumed. Values outside 0 .. 0x10FFFF (including overflow) become Rune(0). Numeric zero is also Rune(0), matching the old API.

The tables are immutable, so lookup is thread-safe. entityToUtf8 allocates its result string.

func entityToRune(entity: openArray[char]): Rune {....raises: [], tags: [],
    forbids: [].}

Converts an entity body to a Rune. Returns Rune(0) when unknown.

See the string overload for the accepted forms.

Example:

import std/unicode
let buffer = "&amp;"
doAssert entityToRune(buffer.toOpenArray(1, 3)) == Rune('&')
func entityToRune(entity: string): Rune {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}

Converts an entity body to a Rune. Returns Rune(0) when unknown.

entity does not include the leading & or the trailing ;. Numeric forms ("#65", "#x41") are supported.

Example:

import std/unicode
doAssert entityToRune("") == Rune(0)
doAssert entityToRune("a") == Rune(0)
doAssert entityToRune("gt") == ">".runeAt(0)
doAssert entityToRune("Uuml") == "Ü".runeAt(0)
doAssert entityToRune("quest") == "?".runeAt(0)
doAssert entityToRune("#x0003F") == "?".runeAt(0)
func entityToUtf8(entity: openArray[char]): string {....raises: [], tags: [],
    forbids: [].}
Converts an entity body to UTF-8. Returns "" when unknown.

Example:

let buffer = "&gt;"
doAssert entityToUtf8(buffer.toOpenArray(1, 2)) == ">"
func entityToUtf8(entity: string): string {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}

Converts an entity body to UTF-8. Returns "" when unknown.

entity does not include the leading & or the trailing ;. Numeric forms ("#65", "#x41") are supported.

Example:

const sigma = "Σ"
doAssert entityToUtf8("") == ""
doAssert entityToUtf8("a") == ""
doAssert entityToUtf8("gt") == ">"
doAssert entityToUtf8("Uuml") == "Ü"
doAssert entityToUtf8("quest") == "?"
doAssert entityToUtf8("#63") == "?"
doAssert entityToUtf8("Sigma") == sigma
doAssert entityToUtf8("#931") == sigma
doAssert entityToUtf8("#0931") == sigma
doAssert entityToUtf8("#x3A3") == sigma
doAssert entityToUtf8("#x03A3") == sigma
doAssert entityToUtf8("#x3a3") == sigma
doAssert entityToUtf8("#X3a3") == sigma
